mainTopic: Who may lead prayers, read from the תורה, or do נשיאת כפים, and improper practices with תפילין
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing an earlier discussion. Even according to רבה בר שימי, who explains the rule as a way to avoid quarrels, the משנה's case of a קטן works, because his father or teacher could be drawn into a quarrel. Next, אביי rules that a קטן פוחח may not read from the תורה, because the reason is כבוד צבור. The חכמים and רבי יהודה then argue whether a סומא may lead פורס על שמע. רבי יוסי's story of the blind man with a torch shows that even a blind person benefits from light. A new משנה follows, barring a כהן with blemished or dyed hands from נשיאת כפים, and the גמרא adds more cases: spotted hands, mixing up letters, runny eyes and blindness in one eye. A כהן who is דש בעירו, or whose dyed hands are common in his town, may still bless, since people will not stare. Another משנה bars a prayer leader who insists on white clothes or bare feet, because he may be influenced by מינות. It also lists improper ways of making and wearing תפילין, and רב פפא explains that 'round' there means ball-shaped. A new משנה begins at the end and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The quarrel concern applies here too
steps.stepSummary: According to רבה בר שימי, the case under discussion still carries a risk that the child's father or teacher may quarrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, there is a concern that his father or teacher will quarrel if someone else is chosen to lead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the earlier discussion. It shows that in this case, רבה בר שימי's reason (avoiding a quarrel) still applies, because the person's father or teacher is involved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, two reasons were given for the rule: honor (רב פפא) and avoiding a quarrel (רבה בר שימי). The משנה also rules that if the מפטיר is a קטן, his father or teacher leads in his place. That seems hard for רבה בר שימי, since a child is not one to quarrel. This line answers that the quarrel concern applies to the father or teacher instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too — the same reasoning applies to this case

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה בר שימי, the rule exists to prevent quarrels. That reason also covers the case where a קטן's father or teacher leads in his place.

phrases.english: Here too,
phrases.notes: He's taking רבה בר שימי's reasoning and using it for our case.

phrases.english: there is the quarreling of his father
and the quarreling of his teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, אִיכָּא נִצּוּיֵי אָבִיו וְנִצּוּיֵי רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion by showing that רבה בר שימי's quarrel reason also explains the משנה's case of a קטן, whose father or teacher leads in his place.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even in this case, רבה בר שימי's concern still applies: the child's father or teacher may quarrel.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about a person with exposed limbs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites the משנה: a פוחח may lead פורס על שמע (and translate), but may not read from the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: A person whose limbs are exposed may lead the blessings of שמע, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה. This is a setup step that prepares the question coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה says a פוחח may lead פורס על שמע and translate, but may not read from the תורה. The words וכו׳ point to that ending, which is what the next question is about.

keyTerms.meaning: A person dressed in torn clothing, with parts of his body exposed
Leading the congregation in the blessings of קריאת שמע
Etc. — the rest of the quoted line

phrases.english: One whose limbs are exposed may lead the blessings of Shema, etc.
phrases.notes: This is quoting the משנה, which goes on: but he may not read from the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פוחח may lead פורס על שמע but may not read from the תורה.

steps.title: May a minor with exposed limbs read from the Torah?
steps.stepSummary: עולא בר רב asks אביי whether a קטן who is פוחח may read from the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא בר רב asked אביי: A minor whose limbs are exposed — may he read from the תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: עולא בר רב asks a real question. He wants to know if the rule against a פוחח reading also applies to a child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קטן is normally allowed to read from the תורה. The thinking behind the question is that a child's uncovered body may not count as indecent, so the ban on a פוחח might not apply to him.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked of him (introduces a question)

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ עוּלָּא בַּר רַב מֵאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Ulla bar Rav asked of Abaye:
a minor whose limbs are exposed —
what is the law, may he read from the Torah?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ עוּלָּא בַּר רַב מֵאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the משנה's rule about a פוחח reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the ban on a פוחח reading from the תורה also apply to a קטן?

steps.title: אביי: the reason is respect for the congregation
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that even a fully naked child may not read, because of כבוד צבור. The same reason forbids a קטן פוחח.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Then ask the same about a naked minor! Why can't a naked minor read? Because of respect for the congregation. Here too, it is because of respect for the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers with a sharp comparison. Everyone agrees a naked child cannot read, so a child with exposed limbs cannot read either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי changes the reason behind the rule. It is not about the reader's own state of modesty. It is about the dignity of the congregation, so the reader's age makes no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Then you should also ask about… (a rhetorical push-back)

steps.whatToRemember: A פוחח may not read from the תורה because of כבוד צבור. That reason applies to a קטן as well.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not really telling עולא בר רב to ask about a naked child. The obvious answer for a naked child is meant to settle the question about a פוחח child.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Then ask the same about a naked minor!
phrases.notes: He's not really asking; the answer there is obvious.

phrases.english: A naked one — why may he not read?
because of respect for the congregation;
here too, it is because of respect for the congregation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers עולא בר רב's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קטן פוחח may not read, because the ban is based on כבוד צבור, just like the ban on a naked child.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about a blind person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites the משנה: a סומא may lead פורס על שמע. רבי יהודה disagrees about someone who never saw the luminaries.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: A blind person may lead the blessings of שמע, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. This is a setup step for the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה continues: רבי יהודה says that anyone who never saw the luminaries in his life may not lead פורס על שמע. That is because the first blessing, יוצר המאורות, praises God for the lights. The ברייתא that comes next argues against רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The luminaries (sun, moon, stars), the topic of the first blessing before שמע

phrases.english: A blind person may lead the blessings of Shema, etc.
phrases.notes: This is quoting the משנה, including the part where רבי יהודה disagrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא says a סומא may lead פורס על שמע. רבי יהודה forbids someone who never saw the luminaries.

steps.title: The Sages answer רבי יהודה with the example of the Divine Chariot
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that the חכמים told רבי יהודה: many have expounded the מרכבה without ever seeing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a baraita: They said to רבי יהודה: Many have looked deeply enough to expound the Divine Chariot, yet they never saw it in their lives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which the חכמים argue against רבי יהודה's view about a blind person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's logic is that you cannot bless over something you never saw. The חכמים answer that understanding does not require seeing: people expound the מרכבה deeply without ever having seen it. So a blind person can also praise God for the luminaries.
steps.whyThisMatters: This argument supports the view that a blind person may lead פורס על שמע, which is the accepted position of the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: It was taught: They said to Rabbi Yehuda:
Many have perceived enough to expound the Divine Chariot,
and they never saw it in their lives.
phrases.notes: So seeing is not needed in order to praise

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that challenges רבי יהודה's view from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that someone who never saw the luminaries may not lead פורס על שמע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: People expound the מרכבה without ever seeing it, so seeing with one's eyes is not required in order to praise God for something.

steps.title: רבי יהודה explains why the מרכבה proof does not apply
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers the חכמים: the מרכבה depends on understanding, but the ברכה on the luminaries depends on benefit, and a blind person does not benefit from light.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does רבי יהודה answer? There, with the מרכבה, everything depends on the understanding of the heart, and a person can concentrate and understand it without seeing it. Here, the ברכה is said because of the benefit from the light, and a blind person gets no benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יהודה against the challenge from step 6. It shows that the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים argued that you do not need to see something in order to speak about it, since people expounded the מרכבה without seeing it. רבי יהודה answers that the comparison fails. Studying the מרכבה is a mental activity, but the ברכה of יוצר המאורות is a thank-you for benefit, and he holds that a blind person has none.

keyTerms.meaning: Understanding of the heart; grasping something in the mind
Benefit, the reason a ברכה is said

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is not saying a blind person cannot understand the luminaries. He agrees understanding is possible without sight. His point is that this ברכה is about benefit, not understanding.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda (how does he respond?)
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking: how does רבי יהודה deal with the חכמים' proof?

phrases.english: There, on the understanding of the heart
phrases.notes: "There" means the case of the מרכבה.

phrases.english: the matter depends
and he can concentrate and understand it.
Here, it is because of benefit,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the blessing over the luminaries.

phrases.english: and he (the blind man) has no benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הָתָם בְּאֹבַנְתָּא דְלִיבָּא תַּלְיָא מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי יהודה against the challenge from the מרכבה in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (חילוק): understanding-based versus benefit-based.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Speaking about something you never saw is always allowed, as with the מרכבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברכה on the luminaries is a benefit-based ברכה, so a person who gets no benefit cannot say it.

steps.title: The Rabbis hold that a blind person does benefit from light
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reply that a blind person does get benefit from light, following רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן hold that he does have benefit, like רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's answer to רבי יהודה's argument. It also sets up a source from רבי יוסי that will prove their point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן accept רבי יהודה's rule that this ברכה is about benefit. They disagree only about the facts: they claim a blind person also benefits from light. The proof comes in the next steps.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis: he does have benefit,
in accordance with Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן — אִית לֵיהּ הֲנָאָה, כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's counter-position to רבי יהודה's reasoning in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual disagreement: they accept the benefit principle but deny that a blind person lacks benefit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A blind person gets nothing from light.
steps.terutzMaskana: A blind person does benefit from light, as רבי יוסי will show.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's puzzle about the verse of the groping blind man
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי, who was bothered by a פסוק that speaks of a blind man groping in the dark: why would darkness matter to someone who cannot see?
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי יוסי said, All my life I was troubled by this verse: "And you shall grope at noon as the blind man gropes in the darkness." What difference does it make to a blind man whether it is dark or light?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source behind the רבנן's view. רבי יוסי first states his puzzle, which sets up the story in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק suggests that darkness makes things worse for a blind man. That seems strange, since a blind man cannot see either way. This question sets up the answer that a blind person does gain something from light.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yosei said:
All my days I was troubled
by this verse:
"And you shall grope at noon
as the blind man gropes in the darkness."
But what does it matter to a blind man
whether it is dark or light?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: כׇּל יָמַי הָיִיתִי מִצְטַעֵר עַל מִקְרָא זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the ברייתא cited to support the רבנן in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The רבנן's claim that a blind person benefits from light.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יוסי on דברים 28:29.

steps.title: The blind man with the torch
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי met a blind man carrying a torch at night. The man explained that the torch lets others see him and save him from pits and thorns, so even a blind person benefits from light.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until a story happened to me. Once I was walking in the pitch dark of night, and I saw a blind man walking on the road with a torch in his hand. I said to him: My son, why do you need this torch? He said to me: As long as the torch is in my hand, people see me and save me from the pits, the thorns, and the thistles.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי answers his own puzzle with a real-life story. This completes the proof for the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blind man cannot see the light himself, but the light still helps him, because others can see him and guide him away from danger. So a blind person does get indirect benefit from light. That is why, according to the רבנן, he may say יוצר המאורות and lead פורס על שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a story that happened
The darkest part of the night

steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, a סומא may lead פורס על שמע, because even a blind person benefits from light, since others see him and protect him.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that indirect benefit counts as real benefit for saying a ברכה.

phrases.english: until an incident came to my hand:
Once I was walking
in the pitch black of night and darkness,
and I saw a blind man
who was walking on the road
with a torch in his hand.
I said to him: My son,
why do you need this torch?
He said to me:
As long as the torch is in my hand,
people see me
and save me from the pits
and from the thorns and from the thistles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוסי's puzzle from step 9 and completes the proof for the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why darkness would matter to a blind person (asked in step 9).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Light lets others see the blind person and protect him, so he does benefit from it.

steps.title: New משנה: a כהן with blemished or dyed hands
steps.stepSummary: A כהן with blemishes on his hands may not do נשיאת כפים. רבי יהודה adds that even a כהן whose hands are dyed with סטיס may not, because people will stare at him.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A כהן who has blemishes on his hands may not lift his hands for ברכת כהנים. רבי יהודה says: Even one whose hands are dyed with סטיס (a blue dye) may not lift his hands, because the people will stare at him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins on a new topic, which kinds of כהנים may not do נשיאת כפים. The גמרא will discuss it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is that unusual-looking hands draw the congregation's eyes, and people should not stare at the כהנים during the ברכה. The תנא קמא speaks only of physical blemishes. רבי יהודה extends the rule to hands that are merely stained.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A priest who has blemishes on his hands
may not lift his hands.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even one whose hands were
dyed with satis (blue dye)
may not lift his hands,
because the people will look at him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֵן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּיָדָיו מוּמִין לֹא יִשָּׂא אֶת כַּפָּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the סומא discussion is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן with blemished hands may not do נשיאת כפים. רבי יהודה extends this to dyed hands, because people will stare.

steps.title: Which blemishes count: face, hands, and feet
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the מומין mentioned in the משנה are only those on the face, hands, and feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A ברייתא teaches: The blemishes that the חכמים spoke about are blemishes on his face, his hands, and his feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה by quoting a ברייתא that defines which blemishes stop a כהן from doing נשיאת כפים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just said 'blemishes' without saying where. The ברייתא limits it to places people can see while the כהנים bless. The worry is that people will stare, so a hidden blemish does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion explaining the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Feet are on the list because the כהנים went up barefoot, so their feet could be seen. Not every blemish anywhere on the body counts.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
The blemishes that they spoke of
are on his face, his hands, and his feet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the word 'blemishes' from the משנה in step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only blemishes on the visible areas (face, hands, feet) disqualify a כהן from נשיאת כפים.

steps.title: Spotted hands disqualify
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that a כהן whose hands have white spots may not do נשיאת כפים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: If his hands have white spots, he may not lift his hands to bless.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives a specific example of a hand blemish that disqualifies a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spots on the hands are not a serious defect, but they are exactly what people notice when the כהן raises his hands. So this fits the reason that people will stare at him.

keyTerms.meaning: Covered with white spots or blotches
He may not lift his hands, i.e., may not do נשיאת כפים

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
If his hands are spotted with white blotches,
he may not lift his hands to bless.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a concrete example of a hand blemish
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן with spotted hands may not do נשיאת כפים.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the ruling and adds crooked hands
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same rule about spotted hands and adds that bent or crooked hands also disqualify.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: If his hands are spotted, he may not lift his hands. If they are curved or bent, he may not lift his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that a ברייתא says the same thing as רבי יהושע בן לוי, which supports him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תניא נמי הכי' means a תנאית source backs up the אמורא. The ברייתא also adds another case: hands that are curved inward or bent sideways, which people would also stare at.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this (a support)

phrases.english: It was also taught in a ברייתא like this:

phrases.aramaic: יָדָיו בּוֹהֲקָנִיּוֹת — לֹא יִשָּׂא אֶת כַּפָּיו.
phrases.english: If his hands are spotted, he may not lift his hands.

phrases.aramaic: עֲקוּמּוֹת עֲקוּשׁוֹת — לֹא יִשָּׂא אֶת כַּפָּיו.
phrases.english: If they are curved or crooked, he may not lift his hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 13 from a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule about spotted hands
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that states the same rule and adds crooked hands

steps.title: People from חיפה and בית שאן may not bless
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי rules that a כהן from חיפה or בית שאן may not do נשיאת כפים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: A כהן from חיפה or from בית שאן may not lift his hands to bless.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from body blemishes to a speech problem that also disqualifies a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People from these towns could not pronounce certain letters properly. The problem is not how the כהן looks but that the words of the blessing come out wrong. The next step explains exactly what the problem was.

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:

phrases.aramaic: חֵיפָנִי וּבֵישָׁנִי — לֹא יִשָּׂא אֶת כַּפָּיו.
phrases.english: A man from Haifa or Beit She'an may not lift his hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new kind of disqualification: speech, not appearance
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים from חיפה and בית שאן may not do נשיאת כפים.

steps.title: A ברייתא: they mix up א and ע
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says people from בית שאן, חיפה, and טבעונין may not lead the prayers because they say א as ע and ע as א.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: We do not send people from בית שאן, from חיפה, or from טבעונין to lead the prayers before the ark, because they read א as ע and ע as א.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רב אסי with a ברייתא and shows the reason: these people mix up letters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about leading the תפילה, not about נשיאת כפים. But the same reason applies: mixing up א and ע changes the meaning of the words. So if they cannot lead prayers, they also cannot say ברכת כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Send down before the ark, i.e., appoint to lead the prayers

phrases.english: It was also taught like this:
We do not send down before the ark to lead prayers
not the people of Beit She'an,
nor the people of (Beit) Haifa,
nor the people of Tivonin,
because they pronounce alef as ayin
and ayin as alef.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אסי from a ברייתא and explains the reason
steps.raayaObject: רב אסי's rule about people from חיפה and בית שאן
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא forbidding them to lead prayers because they mix up א and ע

steps.title: רבי חייא teases רבי שמעון about his thick voice
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא tells רבי שמעון the son of רבי that if he were a לוי, his thick voice would disqualify him from singing on the דוכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said to רבי שמעון the son of רבי: If you were a לוי, you would be disqualified from the platform, because your voice is thick.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a side story connected to speech and voice flaws. This step sets up the reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לויים sang in the בית המקדש on a platform called the דוכן, and a good voice was needed. רבי חייא points out that רבי שמעון's thick voice would not be good enough. The story continues the theme that how a person sounds can matter for holy service.

keyTerms.meaning: If only, if it were the case
The platform where the לויים sang in the מקדש

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya said to
Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi:
If you were a Levite,
you would be disqualified from the platform,
because your voice is thick.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story continuing the theme of speech and voice flaws
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thick voice would disqualify a לוי from singing on the דוכן.

steps.title: רבי answers back: your own pronunciation is worse
steps.stepSummary: רבי tells his son to reply that when רבי חייא reads 'וחכיתי לה׳', he says it with a ה and ends up saying something insulting to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון went and told his father. רבי said to him: Go tell him: When you reach the verse 'וְחִכִּיתִי לַה׳' (I will wait for ה׳), aren't you blaspheming?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives his son a sharp reply to רבי חייא, pointing out a pronunciation flaw of his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא came from בבל and could not tell ח apart from ה. So 'וחכיתי' (I will wait) came out as 'והכיתי' (I will strike), which sounds like an insult to ה׳. The point is that רבי חייא's flaw is worse than a thick voice, because it changes the meaning of the words.

keyTerms.meaning: And I will wait (with ח); with ה it means 'and I will strike'

steps.confusionAlert: רבי חייא was not really blaspheming. רבי is pointing out that his accent changes ח into ה, so the word sounds like 'I will strike'.

phrases.english: He came and told his father.
He said to him: Go say to him:
When you reach the verse 'And I will wait for the Lord,'
won't you turn out to be insulting and blaspheming?!
phrases.notes: Because he says ה instead of ח: 'and I will strike'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replies to רבי חייא's remark in step 17
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to answer רבי חייא's comment about the thick voice
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי חייא himself mixes up ח and ה, which is a worse flaw because it changes the meaning of a פסוק.

steps.title: A כהן with runny eyes may not bless
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a כהן whose eyes always run with tears may not do נשיאת כפים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: A כהן whose eyes run may not lift his hands to bless.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to visible blemishes and gives another case: eyes that always drip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Runny eyes are on the face, so they fit the ברייתא's list of visible places in step 12. People would look at him instead of focusing on the ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: A person whose eyes constantly run with tears

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
One whose eyes run may not lift his hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to visible blemishes after the speech section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זבלגן may not do נשיאת כפים.

steps.title: But a man near רב הונא did bless
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא: there was a כהן with runny eyes in his own neighborhood who did נשיאת כפים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't there a certain man in רב הונא's neighborhood who had this condition, and he would spread his hands to bless?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's rule using a real-life case from right next to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב הונא really held that a זבלגן may not bless, he would not have let this neighbor do it. What actually happened seems to contradict his ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)
Spreads his hands, i.e., does נשיאת כפים

phrases.english: But wasn't there a certain man
who was in Rav Huna's neighborhood,
and he would spread his hands to bless!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הַהוּא דַּהֲוָה בְּשִׁיבָבוּתֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's ruling in step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that a זבלגן may not bless
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A זבלגן in רב הונא's own neighborhood did bless, which seems to show it is allowed.

steps.title: He was well known in his town
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the neighbor was familiar to everyone in town, so nobody stared at him.
steps.simpleTranslation: That man was well known in his town.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the neighbor was a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole reason for the rule is that people will stare. If everyone in town already knows him and is used to his condition, they will not stare. So the rule still stands, but this case is an exception.

keyTerms.meaning: Familiar in his town; people are used to him

phrases.english: That man was a familiar figure in his town.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the rule's reason does not apply here
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The neighbor's blessing shows a זבלגן may always bless.
steps.terutzMaskana: A זבלגן may not bless, unless he is familiar in his town, since then people do not stare.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms the exception
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a זבלגן may not bless, but if he is familiar in his town, he is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: A person whose eyes run may not lift his hands, but if he is familiar in his town, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up both רב הונא's rule and the answer about a familiar person with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says both parts together: the basic rule and the exception. This shows the answer in step 21 was not invented just to get out of a problem. It was already taught by the תנאים.
steps.whatToRemember: A כהן with a visible blemish (face, hands, feet) or bad pronunciation may not do נשיאת כפים, because people will stare or the words will come out wrong. For a visible blemish that draws stares, familiarity in town can permit נשיאת כפים. Bad pronunciation is a separate problem: familiarity does not fix words that come out wrong.
steps.whyThisMatters: The reason behind the rule (people staring) also decides when the rule does not apply. This is why a familiar כהן is allowed to bless.

phrases.english: It was also taught like this:
One whose eyes run may not lift his hands,
but if he was familiar in his town, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב הונא and the answer in step 21
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's rule and the exception for one who is דש בעירו
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating both the rule and the exception
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A זבלגן may not bless, but if he is familiar in his town he may.

steps.title: A כהן blind in one eye may not bless
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that a כהן who is blind in one eye may not do נשיאת כפים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: A כהן who is blind in one eye should not raise his hands to bless the people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבי יוחנן, similar to רב הונא's rule about runny eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is the same as before. People will stare at the כהן's unusual eye during the blessing, and that distracts them from the ברכה. So a visible blemish on the face keeps him from blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: The priestly blessing (literally, raising the hands)
He may not raise his hands, meaning he may not bless

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who is blind in one of his eyes
may not lift his hands (to bless).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to רב הונא's ruling in step 19, now about a different eye blemish.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן blind in one eye may not do נשיאת כפים.

steps.title: But a כהן in his own neighborhood did bless
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: a one-eyed כהן in רבי יוחנן's own neighborhood used to bless.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't there a certain כהן in רבי יוחנן's neighborhood who was blind in one eye, and he used to spread his hands and bless?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's rule with a real-life case from right near him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a one-eyed כהן blessed right in רבי יוחנן's neighborhood, it seems רבי יוחנן allowed it. That looks like it contradicts his own ruling. This is the same pattern as the challenge to רב הונא in step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that…? (opens a challenge)
He would spread his hands (to bless)

phrases.english: But wasn't there a certain one who was
in the neighborhood of Rabbi Yochanan
who would spread his hands (and bless)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that a one-eyed כהן may not bless.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known case in רבי יוחנן's own area shows a one-eyed כהן blessing, which seems to contradict the rule.

steps.title: He was familiar in his town
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this כהן was well known in town, so nobody stared at him.
steps.simpleTranslation: That כהן was familiar in his town.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by showing that this case is an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule exists because people stare. Everyone already knew this כהן and was used to his eye, so they would not look at him during the blessing. The rule stays in place, and familiarity is the exception.

keyTerms.meaning: Familiar in his town (literally, 'well-trodden'), so people are used to how he looks

phrases.english: That one was familiar in his town.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (exception based on the reason behind the rule)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The neighbor's blessing seemed to show that one-eyed כהנים may bless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule stands. A כהן who is familiar in his town is an exception because people won't stare.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the familiar-in-town exception
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states both the rule and the exception for a one-eyed כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: A כהן blind in one eye may not bless, but if he is familiar in his town, he is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what it just answered, which confirms the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spells out both parts: the basic rule and the familiar-in-town exception. So the answer in step 25 was not a forced excuse; it is an earlier taught law.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא (a supporting source)

steps.whatToRemember: For a blemish that draws stares, the rule is: no נשיאת כפים, unless the כהן is familiar in town (דש בעירו).

phrases.english: It was also taught so (in a baraita):
One who is blind in one of his eyes
may not lift his hands,
but if he was familiar in his town
he is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 25.
steps.raayaObject: The exception that a familiar כהן may bless despite being blind in one eye.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating the rule and the exception explicitly.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a כהן with dyed hands may not bless
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling of רבי יהודה that a כהן with colored hands may not bless.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: A כהן whose hands are stained with dye may not raise his hands to bless.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה to set up the next comment about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stained hands would catch people's eyes when the כהן raises them during the blessing. It is the same staring concern as the eye blemishes.

keyTerms.meaning: His hands are dyed or colored (for example, from working with dyes)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One whose hands were colored
may not lift his hands.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Quotation of the משנה (setup for the next step)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יהודה's clause in the משנה (step 11) about dyed hands, after the discussion of the תנא קמא's blemishes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן with dyed hands may not do נשיאת כפים.

steps.title: Exception when most townspeople are dyers
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if most people in town work with dye, a כהן with dyed hands may bless.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: If most people in the town work at this job (dyeing), he is allowed to bless.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא adds an exception to רבי יהודה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If dyed hands are normal in that town, nobody will notice them. The reason for the rule (staring) is missing, so the rule does not apply. This matches the familiar-in-town exception from before.
steps.whatToRemember: All these blemish rules follow one idea: the problem is people staring, so where people won't stare, the כהן may bless.

phrases.english: It was taught (in a baraita):
If most of the people of the town
have this as their work, he is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dyed hands do not disqualify a כהן if most of the town works with dye.

steps.title: One who refuses to lead prayers in colored clothes or sandals
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: someone who refuses to lead prayers in colored clothes or in sandals may not lead at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone says, 'I will not lead the prayers in colored clothes,' he may not lead even in white clothes. If he says, 'I will not lead in sandals,' he may not lead even barefoot.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says that a person who insists on strange rules for how to dress when leading prayers is not allowed to lead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Insisting on one specific color or on going barefoot is a sign that the person follows the practices of heretics (מינים). So even in the clothing he chose, we do not let him lead the תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (start of a new משנה)
Passing before the ark, meaning leading the prayers as שליח ציבור

steps.confusionAlert: He is not barred because white clothes or bare feet are bad. He is barred because his insistence shows he may be a heretic.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who says: I will not pass before the ark
in colored garments
may not pass even in white ones.
(If he says:) In a sandal I will not pass
he may not pass even barefoot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who insists on specific clothing or footwear for leading prayers is disqualified from leading at all.

steps.title: Round תפילין: danger and no מצוה
steps.stepSummary: Making round תפילין puts a person in danger and does not fulfill the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who makes his תפילין round puts himself in danger, and he does not fulfill the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a wrong way of making תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תפילין must be square. Round ones do not fulfill the מצוה. In times of persecution, the person can still be caught wearing them, so he takes the risk and gets nothing for it.

phrases.english: One who makes his tefillin round
there is danger, and there is no מצוה in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next clause of the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Round תפילין are invalid and risky.

steps.title: תפילין on the forehead or palm is the way of heretics
steps.stepSummary: Placing תפילין on the forehead or the palm follows the practice of heretics.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he put the head תפילין on his forehead, or the hand תפילין on his palm, this is the way of the heretics.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists a wrong placement of תפילין and says it shows heresy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים teach that the head תפילין go above the hairline and the arm תפילין go on the upper arm. Reading the פסוק literally ('between your eyes', 'on your hand') and ignoring that tradition is what the מינים did.

keyTerms.meaning: The way of heresy (rejecting the Oral Torah)

phrases.english: If he placed it on his forehead
or on the palm of his hand
this is the way of heresy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next clause of the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תפילין on the forehead or palm reflect heretical practice.

steps.title: Gold-plated תפילין or worn on the sleeve is the way of outsiders
steps.stepSummary: Plating תפילין with gold or wearing them on the sleeve is the way of outsiders.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he covered the תפילין with gold, or put them on top of his sleeve, this is the way of the outsiders.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with two more improper practices with תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תפילין must be black, and the arm תפילין must touch the arm directly, under the sleeve. Doing otherwise is the way of people outside the community's tradition (חיצונים).
steps.whatToRemember: This משנה lists practices that look like religious devotion but actually reveal heretics or outsiders, either in leading prayers or in wearing תפילין.

phrases.english: If he plated it with gold
or placed it on his sleeve
this is the way of the outsiders.

steps.triggerLanguage: צִיפָּהּ זָהָב וּנְתָנָהּ עַל בֵּית אוּנְקְלִי שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final clause of the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gold-plated תפילין or תפילין worn over the sleeve reflect the practice of outsiders.

steps.title: Why is this prayer leader disqualified?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the משנה that bars someone who refuses to lead prayers in colored clothes or in sandals.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now begins its discussion of the משנה. It asks why a person who will only lead prayers in white clothes or barefoot is not allowed to lead at all. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave a rule but no reason. Wearing colored clothes or sandals is not forbidden, so it is strange to bar someone for avoiding them. The גמרא wants to know what is actually wrong with this person.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: This refers back to the משנה in step 29 about someone who refuses colored clothes or sandals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה from step 29 to ask for its reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a person who insists on white clothes or bare feet is disqualified from leading prayers.

steps.title: The concern is heresy
steps.stepSummary: We fear this person has been influenced by מינות (heresy), so he may not lead prayers.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are concerned that perhaps heresy has been absorbed into him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: we suspect this person has picked up heretical ideas.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His strict insistence on a particular way of dressing for prayer looks like the practice of heretical groups. We do not let someone we suspect of מינות represent the congregation. So the problem is not his clothing. It is what his insistence suggests about his beliefs.

keyTerms.meaning: Heresy; the beliefs of sectarian groups
Has been 'thrown into' him, meaning he has been influenced by it

steps.whatToRemember: The prayer leader is disqualified because his behavior raises suspicion of מינות, not because of the clothes themselves.

phrases.english: We are concerned that perhaps
heresy has been instilled in him.
phrases.notes: These were practices of heretical groups.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is suspected of having been influenced by heresy.

steps.title: Doesn't the משנה already teach that תפילין must be square?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about round תפילין and suggests it already contains the ברייתא's rule that square תפילין are a הלכה למשה מסיני, along with רבא's explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: One who makes his תפילין round puts himself in danger and does not fulfill the מצוה. Shall we say that this משנה already taught what the רבנן taught in a ברייתא: square תפילין are a הלכה למשה מסיני? And רבא said: they must be square along their seams and along their diagonals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the line from the משנה about round תפילין. It then suggests this line may already teach a known ברייתא: that תפילין must be square.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If round תפילין are invalid, it seems to follow that they must be square. That would make the ברייתא's teaching, and רבא's precise definition of square, unnecessary. The point being pressed is that the ברייתא seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say we already learned it (in the משנה)?
A law handed down orally to משה at סיני

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two layers. The quote about round תפילין is from the משנה. The rule about square תפילין is from a ברייתא. 'בתפרן ובאלכסונן' is רבא's explanation of that ברייתא.

phrases.english: One who makes his phylacteries round
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the משנה from step 30.

phrases.english: is in danger and does not fulfill the מצוה.
Shall we say we have learned here that
which the Rabbis taught:
Square phylacteries
are a law given to Moses from Sinai!
And Rava said:
along their seams and their diagonals!
phrases.notes: The תפילין must be perfectly square: equal sides and equal diagonals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה (round תפילין) and asks whether it overlaps with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the ברייתא that requires square תפילין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה already rules out round תפילין, the square requirement seems to follow from it. That would make the ברייתא and רבא's rule redundant.

steps.title: The משנה means round like a nut
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the משנה only invalidates תפילין shaped like a ball. The requirement of a perfect square is therefore a separate, new teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Our משנה is talking about תפילין made like a nut.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that the משנה's 'round' means fully round, like a ball or nut. It does not teach that תפילין must be square.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only rules out the extreme case of a ball-shaped box. It says nothing about shapes in between, such as slightly rounded or uneven boxes. So the ברייתא and רבא still teach something new: תפילין must be exactly square.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה rules out ball-shaped תפילין. The ברייתא adds that תפילין must be perfectly square, on the sides and the diagonals.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Our mishna refers to ones made
like a nut.
